title: This Beetle Survives 76 Degrees Below Zero

scenes.text: A beetle can survive at seventy-six degrees below zero.
It lives in Alaska, and it spends the winter frozen.
Its body starts freezing at just twenty-one degrees Fahrenheit.
But it makes a special antifreeze, built from sugar and fat instead of protein.
That antifreeze helps keep ice from damaging its cells.
So yes: a beetle that survives seventy-six below.

description:
A beetle can survive at seventy-six degrees below zero.
The Alaska beetle starts freezing at about 21 degrees Fahrenheit, but it makes a sugar-and-fat antifreeze that protects its cells down to minus 60 Celsius.
Could any other animal beat that?
first_comment: What's the coldest you've ever been outside? We'll start: not -76.
